Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testIssue639` constructs a rotation from two vector pairs (u1, u2) and (v1, v2) and asserts the q0 quaternion component of the resulting Rotation instance. The bug report indicates numerical issues that result in NaN values during such rotation creation.

The `Rotation` constructor taking four `Vector3D` parameters was inspected. The constructor first computes the squared norms of all four vectors and rejects zero-norm vectors. It then rescales v1 to have the same norm as u1. After this, it adjusts v2 to maintain scalar products consistent between the u- and v-vectors, employing a somewhat complex algebraic approach involving coefficients `alpha`, `beta`, and scalar products of the u and v vectors.

The constructor continues by computing vector differences and cross products among these vectors, eventually computing a scalar `c` from dot products of cross products. Based on whether c is zero or small, alternate corrective logic attempts to avoid degenerate cases by switching reference vectors. If all these attempts find c=0, it defaults to the identity rotation.

The quaternion vector portion (q1, q2, q3) is computed straightforwardly from cross product components scaled by the inverse of twice c's square root, but the critical computation for the scalar quaternion part q0 divides products of a dot product by twice the squared norm of a vector k. If values involved become extremely small or zero due to numerical instability in the above computations, this division could yield NaN or infinity values.

The provided test uses extremely large and precise vector values, which likely cause subtle floating point instability or cancellation errors in the normalization and scalar product computations in the constructor. The bug report's indications of NaNs align well with this analysis.

This diagnosis suggests that the root cause is numerical instability during the algebraic manipulation of vectors and scalar products in the constructor, especially in the calculation of `alpha`, `beta` (which involve square roots of differences expected positive but susceptible to floating point error), and critical scalar `c` used to compute quaternions.

The critical area to fix would be the constructor method `Rotation(Vector3D, Vector3D, Vector3D, Vector3D)`, likely involving improved numeric safeguards around division, square roots, and handling near-zero scalar products to avoid invalid operations leading to NaN.

Recommended fix locations to stabilize math and avoid division by near-zero or negative values in these computations are mainly within:
- `Rotation.Rotation(Vector3D, Vector3D, Vector3D, Vector3D)`

Additionally, small vector utility improvements could help but are lower priority here.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
